insight.title: Fish Schools Coordinate Instantly Using Pressure Waves
insight.subtitle: Thousands of fish can pivot in perfect unison without looking at each other, guided by an invisible grid of touch.
insight.notificationHook: How fish school using invisible touch

sections.text: A school of herring can flash and pivot in a fraction of a second, moving like a single liquid mirror. Yet, they never collide, and no single leader directs the turn.

Every fish uses a specialized sensory organ called the lateral line. This row of microscopic pores detects tiny pressure changes in the water, allowing them to feel their neighbors' movements instantly.
Instead of waiting to see a neighbor turn, each fish reacts to the water displaced by the shift. The entire school becomes a giant, decentralized nervous system operating at the speed of touch.
They do not follow a leader; they follow the water.
